Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes

Dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity

Arithmetic limiting laws connect number theory, fractal geometry, Fourier analysis and information theory. The monograph studies their dimensions, sharp concentration, arithmetic convergence and Fourier amplitudes, and proves absolute continuity for logarithmic prime increments.

Independent branches study determinant-constrained decision LWE and cyclotomic lattice smoothing. Arithmetic applications include certified searches for fully splitting negacyclic NTT primes; their cryptographic context is explained below.

Read the monographPDFExplore the results

“Proved” denotes a result stated and proved in the monograph; it does not by itself assert historical priority.

Proved in the monographDimension zero and normal Liouville samples.

The classical shifted-prime totient law has full support on [0,12][0,21​] but Hausdorff dimension zero and packing dimension one. Its samples are almost surely absolutely normal and Liouville.

Proved in the monographSharp concentration and localization.

For the shifted-prime totient law, sharp concentration constants are determined, and every sufficiently short maximizing interval contains 1331​.

Proved in the monographFourier amplitudes and random Euler products.

At a uniformly sampled frequency, the normalized Fourier transform of the logarithmic totient law converges in distribution to a circularly symmetric random Euler product.

Proved in the monographErdős–Kátai conjecture disproved.

Strongly additive functions with prime values (log⁡ℓ)−A(logℓ)−A have absolutely continuous integer laws for every A>0A>0, including the conjectured singular range A>2A>2.

01 / The experiment

What are we measuring?

Choose a large prime p. Factor p−1p−1 conceptually. Each distinct prime factor lowers its totient ratio. Repeating this experiment over primes produces a limiting probability law.

Arithmetic starting point

From matrices to a number between 0 and 1221​

Choose an n×nn×n matrix uniformly over the field with p elements. Its determinant is a primitive root when it generates every nonzero field element by taking powers.

c(p)=φ(p−1)p−1∏j≥1(1−p−j)c(p)=p−1φ(p−1)​j≥1∏​(1−p−j)The primitive-root determinant probability as matrix size n tends to infinity.

Euler’s totient φ(m)φ(m) counts the integers from 1 to m that are coprime to m. Write U(p)=φ(p−1)/(p−1)U(p)=φ(p−1)/(p−1). The product in c(p)c(p) tends to 1 as p grows, so c(p)c(p) and U(p)U(p) share the same limiting law.

Lemma 2.16 · Remark 2.17 · Remark 2.18 · Corollary 7.28
02 / Dimensions & digits

Thin in one sense.
Spread out in another.

Different dimensions answer different questions. Full support describes where the law can reach. A carrier describes where its mass actually lives. Neither statement supplies a probability density.

Geometry of the limiting law

Fractal geometry and information theory

0
Hausdorff dimension

All the probability can be carried by a set coverable at arbitrarily small scales with exceptionally little total size. The law is singular continuous: no atoms, yet no density with respect to length.

1
Packing dimension

Every positive-mass Borel set has packing dimension one. The lower and upper local dimensions are 0 and 1 almost everywhere: the behavior changes with scale.

?
Shannon information dimension

Both lower and upper information dimensions lie strictly between 0.5503615 and 0.570489495. Their equality, and the exact value, remain open.

Theorem 1.1 · Theorem 4.22
The same profile for all four laws

All four basic ratio laws and their logarithmic images are singular continuous with Hausdorff dimension zero, with lower and upper local dimensions 0 and 1 almost everywhere and packing dimension one on every positive-mass Borel set; the four ratio laws themselves give full mass to the Liouville numbers, and the logarithmic laws give full mass to the absolutely normal numbers. The local-dimension and packing conclusions survive deleting finitely many prime coordinates and adding an independent countably atomic head, and hold for every fixed-progression totient law; the singularity, dimension-zero and Liouville conclusions persist under fixed positive-probability conditioning on finitely many valuations, including every fixed-progression totient law. None of the four basic laws or their logarithmic images is doubling: the lower regularity dimension is zero and the upper regularity dimension is infinite.

Theorem 3.16 · Corollary 3.17 · Theorem 5.4 · Corollary 5.16
Rényi dimensions, quantization and rate–distortion

For dyadic Rényi dimensions, Dq=1Dq​=1 for 0<q<10<q<1 and Dq=0Dq​=0 for q>1q>1. At q=1q=1, only the stated lower/upper Shannon bounds are established.

For every fixed positive distortion order, quantization dimension is 1. The classical Kawabata–Dembo identity transfers the arithmetic information-dimension bounds to rate–distortion: lower and upper rate–distortion dimensions equal their respective Shannon dimensions.

For μf∗nμf∗n​, both information dimensions increase to 1 (deficit at most 2−n2−n), while every finite convolution power retains Hausdorff dimension zero.

The four totient/divisor-sum laws over integers/shifted primes and their logarithmic images share the displayed bounds. Equality of information dimensions across the two sampling models is proved for each arithmetic function separately; equality between totient and divisor-sum dimensions remains open.

Corollary 3.12 · Corollary 5.15 · Theorem 4.22 · Theorem 4.23

Shannon entropy versus min-entropy

Asymptotic schematic

Take the first B binary digits of 2X2X: ZB=⌊2B+1X⌋ZB​=⌊2B+1X⌋. Shannon entropy measures average information; min-entropy measures the most likely prefix.

Normal digits do not imply uniformly random prefixes. Almost-sure normality describes block frequencies within one infinite expansion. Entropy describes the distribution of finite prefixes across many samples.
Min-entropy and randomness extraction bounds

For deterministic processing of a single ZBZB​, conditional on an independent finite or countable public seed S, the joint total-variation distance from (S,uniform m-bit output)(S,uniform m-bit output) is at least max⁡{pB−2−m,0}max{pB​−2−m,0}, where pBpB​ is the largest input atom.

Here pB=κend/(Blog⁡2)+O(B−2)pB​=κend​/(Blog2)+O(B−2), giving min-entropy log⁡2B+O(1)log2​B+O(1). The bound can vanish for short outputs. For fixed C>0C>0, in the regime B≤λCB≤λC and m≥λm≥λ, it rules out negligible error in the security parameter λ.

This atom belongs to the quantized prefix law; μGμG​ itself has no atoms.

Corollary 11.12
A stronger closure result

Algebraic independence and normal Liouville fields

Absolutely normal means that in every integer base ≥2≥2, every finite digit block has its expected limiting frequency. Liouville means that rational approximations beat every fixed power of the denominator infinitely often. A typical sample from μGμG​ has both properties.

SAMPLE

X1,X2,X3,…X1​,X2​,X3​,…

Take independent samples from the four basic ratio laws.

COMBINE

X1+X2⋅X3X1​+X2​⋅X3​

Use rational coefficients, addition, multiplication and division by nonzero elements.

CONCLUDE

Normal + Liouville

Almost surely every irrational element of the generated field has both properties; its transcendence degree is infinite.

This is a statement about samples from the limiting laws. It does not make each arithmetic value c(p)c(p) normal: the monograph shows that c(p)c(p) is not normal in base p.

Corollary 11.8 · Proposition 11.14
Why algebraic independence matters
Almost surely, the sampled coordinates are algebraically independent over the rationals. This makes the closure statement nontrivial and ensures that nonconstant rational functions in the samples do not collapse to rational values. The existence of absolutely normal Liouville numbers itself is classical; the distributional and closure results are the point here.

Theorem 7.16
Divisor-sum laws and the Fourier-moment method

The integer and shifted-prime logarithmic divisor-sum laws also have concentration of exact order 1/log⁡(1/h)1/log(1/h), even after removing finitely many prime coordinates and adding an independent countably atomic head. For the shifted-prime logarithmic divisor-sum law this order had previously only been stated, without proof, as a consequence of earlier work; the monograph proves it, together with the shifted-prime totient case and the integer divisor-sum case, whose order goes back to Erdős (1974), directly from Fourier-moment bounds of the form (2T)−1∫−TT∣ν^(t)∣rdt≤(AFr2/log⁡T)r(2T)−1∫−TT​∣ν(t)∣rdt≤(AF​r2/logT)r. The sharp constants and maximizing intervals for divisor sums remain open.

Corollary 7.19 · Theorem 7.23 · Theorem 7.10 · Corollary 7.17
Two error metrics, two very different rates

A good approximation depends on the question you ask

Kolmogorov distance: largest counting discrepancy

Look at all thresholds t and take the largest difference between the empirical and model CDFs. In every fixed reduced progression, for U(p)U(p) or c(p)c(p), this error has sharp order 1/log⁡x1/logx. The proof uses a fixed-progression sieve below the Bombieri–Vinogradov level and localized bounds for large smooth parts; the upper constants and thresholds may be ineffective, since ineffectivity enters through the Siegel–Walfisz theorem in the prime-distribution inputs.

dK(empirical,model)≍Q1/log⁡xdK​(empirical,model)≍Q​1/logx

Wasserstein distance: average transport cost

Move probability mass from one distribution to the other and minimize the average distance moved. For unrestricted primes, the laws of U(p)=φ(p−1)/(p−1)U(p)=φ(p−1)/(p−1) and c(p)c(p), and their negative-logarithmic images, converge faster than every fixed inverse power of log⁡xlogx.

W1(empirical,model)=OB((log⁡x)−B)W1​(empirical,model)=OB​((logx)−B)For every fixed B>0B>0; the constant and threshold may be ineffective.

The Wasserstein rate uses Ford’s approximation of the prime divisors of shifted primes. Unconditionally W1W1​ is at least of order x−1/2/log⁡2xx−1/2/log2x, and under GRH for Dirichlet L-functions it is ≪εexp⁡(−(12−ε)log⁡x⋅log⁡log⁡x)≪ε​exp(−(21​−ε)logx⋅loglogx​) for every fixed 0<ε<120<ε<21​, so the true rate lies between a polynomial lower bound and a conditional sub-exponential upper bound.

The finite-product explorer above demonstrates a related contrast: small W1W1​ error can coexist with a visible endpoint atom. These are separate approximation problems, with separate rates.

Theorem 7.37 · Proposition 7.41 · Proposition 7.42
Convolution modes, quantile sensitivity and fixed thresholds

For each fixed convolution power of the shifted-prime logarithmic totient law, the monograph determines the sharp concentration constant and a finite set of arithmetic mode anchors. Two copies have the unique mode anchor log⁡6log6; four have log⁡45log45. This does not assert uniqueness of a maximizing interval.

The global modulus of the raw quantile function has a different scale from the shortest-interval width: it is governed by the small-value tail.

For unrestricted primes, every fixed rational threshold, and every fixed irrational threshold satisfying the stated finite Diophantine condition, has CDF error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log⁡xlogx. A threshold approaching 1331​ nevertheless realizes discrepancy asymptotic to κend/log⁡xκend​/logx.

Theorem 7.25 · Theorem 7.29 · Proposition 7.38
04 / Fourier behavior & phase transitions

Change the jumps.
Change the kind of law.

The logarithm of the totient model is a prime-indexed Bernoulli convolution: a random sum of independent Bernoulli-weighted jumps about 1/ℓ1/ℓ. Larger, logarithmically decreasing jumps produce an absolutely continuous law, even in the range of the Erdős–Kátai singularity conjecture.

Proved in the monograph

Disproving the Erdős–Kátai singularity conjecture

In 1979, Erdős and Kátai conjectured that the strongly additive function with prime values fA(ℓ)=(log⁡ℓ)−AfA​(ℓ)=(logℓ)−A has a singular limiting distribution over the integers when A>2A>2.

The monograph proves absolute continuity for every A>0A>0, disproving this prediction. It also proves absolute continuity for the limiting distribution of fA(p−1)fA​(p−1) over primes p.

Earlier, for integer sampling, Babu had proved an L2L2 density for 0<A<20<A<2, and Koukoulopoulos had determined the integer concentration order h1/Ah1/A for A>1A>1. The monograph adds exact Fourier-integrability, Sobolev and CkCk thresholds in A, and a local unboundedness theorem for A>1A>1.

Slow-jump regularity explorer

Exact thresholds

Let fAfA​ be strongly additive, with fA(ℓ)=(log⁡ℓ)−AfA​(ℓ)=(logℓ)−A. Both its integer and shifted-prime limiting laws are absolutely continuous for every A>0A>0.

Absolute continuity means that probabilities are obtained by integrating a density. It does not mean the density is bounded or continuous. Here m is the number of independent copies being added.

Theorem 9.5 · Corollary 11.44
Corollary 11.43

Fourier decay of Rajchman measures

Schematic scales

The Fourier transform measures how well an oscillating wave survives averaging against a distribution. A Rajchman law has Fourier transform tending to zero at high frequency. The original totient laws μGμG​ and μfμf​ are Rajchman.

Which measures and which quantifiers?

The pointwise upper bound applies to μGμG​ and μfμf​, with effective constants and threshold, and in fact to all four basic ratio laws and their logarithmic images. For the raw laws the collision probability P(∣Y−Y′∣≤h)P(∣Y−Y′∣≤h) of two independent samples has exact order 1/log⁡2(1/h)1/log2(1/h), and the mean of ∣μ^∣2∣μ​∣2 over [0,T][0,T] has exact order 1/log⁡2T1/log2T. For μfμf​, lim sup⁡τ→∞(log⁡τ/log⁡log⁡τ)∣μ^f(τ)∣≥1limsupτ→∞​(logτ/loglogτ)∣μ​f​(τ)∣≥1. The typical-amplitude limit in the adjacent panel concerns μfμf​, the logarithmic law. Normality of the samples is derived from Fourier decay through Weyl’s criterion and Wall’s theorem, following Davenport, Erdős and LeVeque.

Write S(τ)=∑ℓ≥3[2(ℓ−2)/(ℓ−1)2][1−cos⁡(τωℓ)]S(τ)=∑ℓ≥3​[2(ℓ−2)/(ℓ−1)2][1−cos(τωℓ​)], the nonnegative dissipation sum. The stronger target S(τ)≥2log⁡log⁡∣τ∣−2log⁡log⁡log⁡∣τ∣−O(1)S(τ)≥2loglog∣τ∣−2logloglog∣τ∣−O(1) would give the sharp-order upper bound O(log⁡log⁡∣τ∣/log⁡∣τ∣)O(loglog∣τ∣/log∣τ∣). The dissipation constant cdisscdiss​ lies in [23,2][32​,2], but knowing cdiss=2cdiss​=2 alone would not settle the second logarithmic term.

The mean of S over [0,T][0,T] is 2log⁡log⁡T+CD+O(1/log⁡T)2loglogT+CD​+O(1/logT) and its variance converges to 12∑ℓ≥3dℓ221​∑ℓ≥3​dℓ2​, with supporting Cesàro-moment computations in Appendix C.

Section 13.1 · Theorem 11.22
Not a classical Bernoulli convolution

Classical Bernoulli convolutions use a geometric sequence of jumps λnλn, and their Fourier decay is governed by the Pisot obstruction studied by Erdős and Salem. Here the jumps ωℓ=log⁡(ℓ/(ℓ−1))≍1/ℓωℓ​=log(ℓ/(ℓ−1))≍1/ℓ are nonlacunary and, together with log⁡2log2, linearly independent over QQ, so by the Kronecker–Weyl theorem the phases τωℓτωℓ​ of any fixed finite set of primes can simultaneously be brought arbitrarily close to any prescribed values modulo 2π2π.

The pointwise bound comes from a Vinogradov-type estimate for prime exponential sums with logarithmic and reciprocal phases. The activation-threshold results rest on cancellation in ∑N<p≤2Neiτωp∑N<p≤2N​eiτωp​ on dyadic prime intervals with ∣τ∣a≤N≤∣τ∣1−δ∣τ∣a≤N≤∣τ∣1−δ, obtained from Vaughan’s identity, Type I and bilinear Type II estimates and exponent pairs; an auxiliary Heath-Brown decomposition reaches the same power saving by a second route. A uniform bound of order N/(log⁡N)AN/(logN)A with A>1A>1 throughout dyadic N∈[log⁡τ,τ1−δ]N∈[logτ,τ1−δ] is shown to be impossible.

Proposition 13.1
06 / Applications & independent branches

From distributions
to certified choices.

The arithmetic results support explicit parameter searches. Independent branches study decision learning with errors (LWE), lattice shells and Gaussian smoothing.

Cryptographic context

Connections to lattice-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC)

These connections concern determinant-constrained LWE, certified searches for fully splitting negacyclic number-theoretic transform (NTT) primes, and Gaussian smoothing estimates for cyclotomic lattices.

LWE is Regev’s learning-with-errors problem. The smoothing parameter is the Micciancio–Regev quantity that governs Gaussian smoothing of a lattice. For N a power of two, fully splitting negacyclic NTT primes q≡1 mod 2Nq≡1mod2N are the moduli for which XN+1=Φ2N(X)XN+1=Φ2N​(X) splits completely over FqFq​, so that the length-N negacyclic number-theoretic transform runs entirely over FqFq​; the monograph cites Pollard for the finite-field transform and Lyubashevsky–Seiler for the negacyclic NTT and this splitting. The ring Zq[X]/(XN+1)Zq​[X]/(XN+1) is the polynomial arithmetic of Ring-LWE and Module-LWE constructions, which use fully splitting moduli in some cases and partially splitting ones in others; the monograph does not itself discuss those constructions.

The results address underlying mathematical problems and parameters. The monograph analyzes no standardized or deployed scheme; its one scheme-specific discussion, in Section 12.5, re-examines the LWE reduction and the prescribed moduli of a published secret-sharing construction, and it establishes neither a new encryption scheme nor the security of any protocol.

Certified randomized search

Negacyclic NTT primes without complete factorization

For a fixed power-of-two transform length N and a rational threshold β>2β>2, the search produces primes q≡1 mod 2Nq≡1mod2N with certified reciprocal determinant density 1/c(q)≤β1/c(q)≤β. It uses partial factorization of q−1q−1 and exact rational bounds.

Polynomial verification and the expected search cost

Certificates have effective polynomial verification cost in log⁡qlogq, and each trial has effective expected polynomial bit cost in log⁡xlogx. For sufficiently large x, independent uniform candidate draws in [x,2x][x,2x] with q≡1 mod 2Nq≡1mod2N yield almost-sure halting and

E[candidate draws]∼log⁡x/[2(1−G(1/β))].E[candidate draws]∼logx/[2(1−G(1/β))].

Here log⁡log is natural, N and β are fixed, and x tends to infinity. The onset of this asymptotic regime may be ineffective. The explorer below is a finite worked example.

Theorem 12.27
Independent algebraic branch

Decision LWE with a prescribed determinant law

Decision learning with errors (LWE) asks one to distinguish noisy linear equations with a hidden secret from uniform random data. The monograph constructs a reduction to matrix LWE whose secret determinant follows a chosen nonzero law.

INPUT
Vector LWE in dimension n−1n−1
REDUCTION
n×nn×n matrix LWE · prescribed nonzero determinant
GUARANTEE
Same error law · advantage loss factor n

For n≥2n≥2 over a prime field, under exact expected-polynomial-time sampling assumptions for the error and determinant laws. The matrix secret is uniform conditional on its determinant. This branch is independent of the limiting-distribution arguments.

Variants and the earlier SYD21 reduction

With exact samplers, the main reduction has expected polynomial overhead and advantage ε/nε/n. Polynomially bounded overhead additionally requires known polynomial sampler cutoffs with negligible total failure probability. Cutoff probability at most δ in each experiment gives advantage at least ε/n−2δε/n−2δ.

A same-dimension variant reduces vector LWE in dimension n to the same determinant-law target with advantage exactly ε/(np)ε/(np) under exact sampling, with the same sampler-cutoff qualification as the main reduction; for n, t and p polynomial in the security parameter this loss is polynomial.

Section 12.5 also re-examines Theorem 10 of the author’s earlier paper with Yeo and Desmedt on LWE-based verifiable secret sharing (SYD21), whose moduli p=2m+1p=2m+1 come from set systems with restricted intersections. The monograph states that its factor-n reduction changes the dimension by one and that its same-dimension factor npnp does not establish the O(n2)O(n2) advantage factor asserted there for unrestricted moduli; that the proof of that theorem specifies no procedure extracting a PRIM-LWE instance from the hidden secrets; and that the bounded-norm determinant encoding of that paper is not shown to produce the uniform primitive-determinant secret the theorem assumes. Neither of the monograph’s reductions establishes the security of that protocol.

Corollary 12.18 · Section 12.5
Secrets with i.i.d. entries, and finite rings

For a fixed prime p and any entry law that is not a point mass, the probability that an n×nn×n matrix with i.i.d. entries has primitive-root determinant differs from cn(p)cn​(p) by an exponentially small amount in n, and its determinant law is exponentially close in total variation to that of a uniform matrix, including the conditional laws on any nonempty set of nonzero values. The monograph gives a direct proof for fixed p that avoids a proposition of Maples shown incorrect by Nguyen and Paquette; the fixed-prime estimate also follows from Lvov’s cokernel–determinant universality. It notes that these total variation bounds give neither a uniform varying-modulus estimate nor a total variation bound for the full matrix or LWE transcript.

The full determinant law over Z/QZZ/QZ is classical, due to Brent and McKay, and Choosuwan, Jitman and Udomkavanich treat finite commutative principal ideal rings. Over any nonzero finite commutative ring with identity, the determinant of a uniform n×nn×n matrix lies in a set A of units with probability ∣A∣/∣R×∣∣A∣/∣R×∣ times ∏i∏j≤n(1−qi−j)∏i​∏j≤n​(1−qi−j​), the outer product running over the residue fields of size qiqi​; in particular the primitive-root determinant fraction over FqFq​ is cn(q)cn​(q) for every prime power q.

Type-A lattice shells and cyclotomic geometry

A lattice shell groups vectors of equal length. Building on Kitaoka’s classical classification of minimal vectors, the appendix treats arbitrary type-A tensor products: it classifies and counts second-shell vectors and determines the third distinct nonzero squared norm, including exceptional cases. 07 / Further contributions

Beyond the scalar examples.

The same arithmetic models lead to exact approximation criteria, joint distributions and comparisons of rare events. These results extend the examples above.

Metric Diophantine approximation

Exactly how close can rational approximations get?

For each of the four basic ratio laws, a prime-series test decides whether a prescribed accuracy is achieved by infinitely many reduced rational approximations, almost surely.

The convergence–divergence criterion

Fix a positive finite-valued function ψ comparable to an eventually nondecreasing function. Then ∣X−a/q∣<q−ψ(q)∣X−a/q∣<q−ψ(q) holds for infinitely many reduced fractions a/qa/q almost surely exactly when the sum ∑ℓ prime1/(ℓψ(ℓ))∑ℓ prime​1/(ℓψ(ℓ)) diverges. If the sum converges, there are almost surely only finitely many such approximations.

In the divergent case, the actual finite-product prefixes already supply infinitely many approximants. For ψ(q)=Clog⁡log⁡q⋅(log⁡log⁡log⁡q)βψ(q)=Cloglogq⋅(logloglogq)β, with fixed C>0C>0, divergence occurs exactly when β≤1β≤1. Each assertion fixes ψ before sampling X.

Almost surely the samples are Liouville but not strong Liouville: along the continued-fraction convergents pn/qnpn​/qn​, lim inf⁡an<∞liminfan​<∞ and lim inf⁡log⁡qn+1/log⁡qn=1liminflogqn+1​/logqn​=1, while lim sup⁡log⁡qn+1/log⁡qn=∞limsuplogqn+1​/logqn​=∞; the divergent case above is realized along prefix convergents.

For same-sign Euler products with independent prime activations κ/p+O(p−2)κ/p+O(p−2), the test becomes ∑p1/[pψ(p)κ]∑p​1/[pψ(p)κ], under the same fixed-function hypotheses. Products of m independent totient variables, or m independent divisor-sum variables, have κ=mκ=m.

Theorem 9.8 · Corollary 9.12
Dependent samples

Normal Liouville fields from fixed shifts

Totient ratios at distinct nonzero shifts of the same prime have explicit joint limiting laws with exact supports and Hausdorff dimension zero. Their coordinates share prime-residue information and need not be independent.

From finite tuples to an infinite field

Use the consistent joint limiting model for countably infinitely many distinct nonzero shifts b1,b2,…b1​,b2​,…, with coordinates X1,X2,…X1​,X2​,… corresponding to φ(p+bj)/(p+bj)φ(p+bj​)/(p+bj​). Almost surely, the field Q(X1,X2,…)Q(X1​,X2​,…) has infinite transcendence degree and every irrational element is both absolutely normal and Liouville.

For each fixed nonconstant rational function with real coefficients in finitely many coordinates, its output law is Rajchman and almost surely absolutely normal. The field assertion uses rational coefficients and holds simultaneously for all its irrational elements.

For the joint logarithmic law of (−log⁡X1,…,−log⁡Xk)(−logX1​,…,−logXk​), every nonzero real linear projection has Fourier transform O(ρ(τ)r)O(ρ(τ)r), where r coefficients are nonzero and ρ(τ)=(log⁡log⁡∣τ∣/log⁡∣τ∣)1/3ρ(τ)=(loglog∣τ∣/log∣τ∣)1/3 for large ∣τ∣∣τ∣. Its law is Rajchman and gives full mass to the absolutely normal numbers. The difference f(p+b)−f(p+c)f(p+b)−f(p+c) at distinct nonzero shifts has a limiting law whose existence and continuity go back to Kátai; the monograph shows that it is singular of dimension zero with support RR and has concentration of order 1/log⁡2(1/h)1/log2(1/h) for every pair of distinct nonzero shifts, an order De Koninck and Kátai had obtained at shift 1. The same corollary recovers the sign asymptotics of Garcia and Luca, also deduced by De Koninck and Kátai: φ(p−1)>φ(p+1)φ(p−1)>φ(p+1) and φ(p−1)<φ(p+1)φ(p−1)<φ(p+1) each hold for asymptotically half of the primes.

Extreme tails

Different sampling, nearly identical rare configurations

For large reciprocal-totient and divisor-sum values, the shifted-prime tail probability is asymptotically t times the integer tail probability at threshold t. Conditioned on that rare event, the full prime-valuation configurations become very close.

The quantitative comparison

For either ratio R=n/φ(n)R=n/φ(n) or R=σ(n)/nR=σ(n)/n in the corresponding limiting models, Pshifted(R>t)=t Pinteger(R>t)[1+ON(t−N)]Pshifted​(R>t)=tPinteger​(R>t)[1+ON​(t−N)] for every fixed N>0N>0 as t→∞t→∞.

The total-variation distance between the two laws of all prime valuations, conditional on R>tR>t, is also ON(t−N)ON​(t−N). This compares the entire conditioned factorization model, not only the resulting ratio.

Theorem 6.10
Support criterion

Deshouillers’ criterion for shifted primes

Let g be a positive multiplicative function whose values g(p−1)g(p−1) have a continuous limiting probability law over primes. The support of that law is exactly the closure of the values g(p−1)g(p−1) at odd primes.

What the criterion adds

An open interval receives positive limiting probability exactly when it contains at least one such arithmetic value. The result applies beyond the particular totient and divisor-sum examples.

The monograph proves this general criterion and records the case 0<g≤10<g≤1 announced earlier by Deshouillers and his related result for p+1p+1, the strongly multiplicative case with 0<g≤10<g≤1 under a continuous limiting law.

The criterion is a corollary of the shifted-prime Erdős–Wintner theorem as stated in the monograph (Theorem 2.7). Its existence criterion, a limiting law along p−1p−1 exactly when the three Erdős–Wintner series converge, and its Euler-product characteristic function are classical: sufficiency is due to Kátai and necessity to Hildebrand, as recorded by Tenenbaum. The monograph proves that the law is then of pure type by the Jessen–Wintner theorem, that it is continuous exactly when ∑h(ℓ)≠01/ℓ∑h(ℓ)=0​1/ℓ diverges, that its support is the closure of the values h(p−1)h(p−1) over odd primes p, and that it is the law of an explicit random series over independent prime valuations.

Corollary 2.8 · Theorem 2.7
Further arithmetic laws

Divisor sums and finite-field extensions

The monograph also studies Fourier amplitudes for divisor-sum laws and distributions of totient ratios associated with finite-field extensions.

Totient and divisor-sum ratios at a common input

The pairs (φ(n)/n,σ(n)/n)(φ(n)/n,σ(n)/n) over integers and (φ(p−1)/(p−1),σ(p−1)/(p−1))(φ(p−1)/(p−1),σ(p−1)/(p−1)) over primes converge to explicit joint laws whose carriers have Hausdorff dimension zero. Every nonconstant rational function of the two coordinates with real coefficients has a singular continuous law of Hausdorff and Fourier dimension zero. Almost surely the two coordinates are algebraically independent over QQ and, simultaneously, every nonconstant rational function of them with rational coefficients takes a Liouville value.

Corollary 5.3
Support and left endpoint of the divisor-sum law

The shifted-prime divisor-sum law has support exactly [3/2,∞)[3/2,∞), on which its distribution function is strictly increasing. Near the left endpoint, with L=log⁡(1/ε)L=log(1/ε), Hσ(3/2+ε)=(κend/2){1/(L+log⁡(3/2))−π2/(12(L+log⁡(3/2))3)+O(L−4)}Hσ​(3/2+ε)=(κend​/2){1/(L+log(3/2))−π2/(12(L+log(3/2))3)+O(L−4)}, half the totient endpoint constant with a shifted logarithm. In a fixed reduced class b mod QbmodQ the support becomes [σ(m)/m,∞)[σ(m)/m,∞) with m=lcm⁡(2,gcd⁡(b−1,Q))m=lcm(2,gcd(b−1,Q)), and the law stays singular continuous of Hausdorff dimension zero.

Theorem 2.20 · Proposition 6.19 · Corollary 6.4
Divisor-sum Fourier amplitudes

For the integer and shifted-prime logarithmic divisor-sum laws, the complex Fourier transform at a uniform frequency in [0,T][0,T], multiplied by log⁡TlogT, converges in distribution to a random Euler product. Every fixed positive absolute moment converges too.

Its factors use one random multiplicative character of the positive rationals, so their higher-valuation phases are dependent.

Theorem 11.26
Three extension-degree regimes

For each fixed degree d≥1d≥1, φ(pd−1)/(pd−1)φ(pd−1)/(pd−1), sampled over prime bases p, has an explicit limiting law of Hausdorff dimension zero carried by Liouville numbers. The same law persists at degrees dr(x)dr(x) whenever r(x)r(x) is prime and tends to infinity, without an upper growth restriction on r(x)r(x).

At fixed degree d, the mass within relative distance ε of the upper endpoint is asymptotic to κd/log⁡τ(d)(1/ε)κd​/logτ(d)(1/ε), where τ(d)τ(d) counts divisors and κd>0κd​>0 is explicit.

Proposition 12.49

If the prime power q is instead fixed and degrees are sampled uniformly from 1,…,D1,…,D, the limiting law of φ(qd−1)/(qd−1)φ(qd−1)/(qd−1) is atomless, has Hausdorff dimension zero and has support [0,φ(q−1)/(q−1)][0,φ(q−1)/(q−1)]. This is a separate model with dependent divisibility indicators. For q=2q=2 these are the totient ratios of the Mersenne numbers 2d−12d−1; existence of the q=2q=2 law goes back to Luca, and Deshouillers and Luca indicated its full support.

The monograph records prior existence and continuity results. It does not assert Fourier decay, normality or a Liouville carrier for the fixed-q degree-sampling law.

How small can c(p)c(p) get?
How do sampled primes behave?

Beyond limiting laws, the monograph gives explicit and effective bounds for the primitive-root determinant density at a single prime, uniform estimates in growing arithmetic progressions, and limit theorems for primes sampled at random, as in residue number systems.

Extremal order, made effective

Random prime bases

Limit theorems for random residue-number-system bases

Sample k distinct primes uniformly without replacement, as in finite-population sampling, from a reduced class modulo a power of two Q=2a≤(log⁡x)AQ=2a≤(logx)A among the primes p≤xp≤x, as when the moduli of a residue number system (RNS) are chosen at random. The sum of −log⁡c(qi)−logc(qi​) over the sample obeys a quantitative central limit theorem of Berry–Esseen type with exact finite-population variance, large-deviation principles for k→∞k→∞ with k/n→0k/n→0 and at a positive sampling fraction k/n→f∈(0,1)k/n→f∈(0,1), and, at such a positive sampling fraction, a moderate-deviation principle and an interval local limit theorem; constants and thresholds may be ineffective.

What the sampling theorems say

Normal approximation. With n primes in the population, empirical mean mxmx​ and variance vxvx​, and θ=(n−k)/(n−1)θ=(n−k)/(n−1), the Kolmogorov distance between (S−kmx)/kθvx(S−kmx​)/kθvx​​ and the standard normal law is at most CA/k(1−k/n)CA​/k(1−k/n)​ uniformly for 1≤k<n1≤k<n, a bound of Berry–Esseen type. So the empirical normalization converges whenever min⁡{k,n−k}→∞min{k,n−k}→∞. Centering at the model mean kμkμ, with μ=E[−log⁡X]μ=E[−logX], is proved for k→∞k→∞ with k≤(log⁡x)Dk≤(logx)D. Under GRH the population range extends to Q=2a≤x1/2−δQ=2a≤x1/2−δ and the model-centered range to k≤xηk≤xη for any fixed η<min⁡{2δ,12+δ}η<min{2δ,21​+δ}.

Large deviations. For k→∞k→∞ with k/n→0k/n→0, the sample sum has the Cramér rate function I of the independent model built from copies of −log⁡X−logX, whose log-moment generating function is K(t)=log⁡M(−t)K(t)=logM(−t). At a positive sampling fraction k/n→fk/n→f, the classical finite-population principle gives a logistic pressure and a rate IfIf​ that is finite exactly on an interval determined by the trimmed means of the limiting law. The proofs use Hájek’s representation of rejective sampling by independent Bernoulli variables conditioned on their sum, with saddlepoint antecedents in Robinson and in Hu, Robinson and Wang.

At a positive sampling fraction, (S−kmn)/(ank)(S−kmn​)/(an​k​) satisfies a moderate-deviation principle with speed an2an2​ and rate z2/(2(1−f)ς2)z2/(2(1−f)ς2) whenever an→∞an​→∞ and an=o(k)an​=o(k​), a range the monograph notes also follows from classical estimates of Hu, Robinson and Wang and of Hoeffding by truncation; as the theorem’s separate contribution, σnσn​ times the probability that S−kmnS−kmn​ falls in a fixed window [z,z+h][z,z+h] is uniformly close to h times the standard normal density at z/σnz/σn​.

The monograph is explicit that these products of reciprocal determinant densities are not by themselves computational costs of an RNS; a multiplicative cost would require a separate sampling model.

Growing moduli

Progression laws when the modulus grows with x

Fixed progressions have sharp Kolmogorov order 1/log⁡x1/logx. The monograph also controls the CDF error when the modulus Q grows with x: unconditionally in several ranges, and under the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for Dirichlet L-functions for every Q≤x1/2−δQ≤x1/2−δ.

Ranges and error terms

Uniformly for Q≤(log⁡x)CQ≤(logx)C and every reduced class b mod QbmodQ, the CDF error is ≪D(Q)log⁡log⁡x/log⁡x≪D(Q)loglogx/logx, where D(Q)=∏ℓ∣Q, ℓ>2(ℓ−1)/(ℓ−2)D(Q)=∏ℓ∣Q, ℓ>2​(ℓ−1)/(ℓ−2). All but O(H(log⁡x)−A)O(H(logx)−A) moduli Q≤H≤x1/2−δQ≤H≤x1/2−δ satisfy the same bound. For powers of two, Elliott’s theorem on fixed-base power moduli gives it unconditionally for every Q=2a≤x1/3exp⁡(−(log⁡log⁡x)3)Q=2a≤x1/3exp(−(loglogx)3).

Under GRH, every Q≤x1/2−δQ≤x1/2−δ has CDF error ≪D(Q)log⁡log⁡x/log⁡x≪(log⁡log⁡x)2/log⁡x≪D(Q)loglogx/logx≪(loglogx)2/logx. For powers of two, the GRH Mellin estimates apply to c(p)c(p) and φ(p−1)/(p−1)φ(p−1)/(p−1).

For the certified NTT search with N a power of two and fixed rational β>2β>2, and q a uniform prime q≡1 mod 2Nq≡1mod2N in [x,2x][x,2x], the acceptance probability P(UB+(q)≤β)P(UB+​(q)≤β) equals 1−G(1/β)+OA((log⁡log⁡log⁡x)−1)1−G(1/β)+OA​((logloglogx)−1) uniformly for 2N≤(log⁡x)A2N≤(logx)A, and the output is within total-variation distance OA,β((log⁡log⁡log⁡x)−1)OA,β​((logloglogx)−1) of a uniformly random prime q≡1 mod 2Nq≡1mod2N in [x,2x][x,2x] with 1/c(q)≤β1/c(q)≤β; constants and thresholds may be ineffective. Theorem 7.39 · Corollary 7.45 · Corollary 7.40 · Theorem 6.3
Proposition 7.43 · Theorem 7.46 · Corollary 12.26 · Theorem A.1 · Theorem A.2
Moments

An entire Mellin transform of order one

The moments E[Xs]E[Xs] of the limiting law extend to an entire function M(s)M(s) of order exactly one and infinite type, given by a convergent Euler product with explicit simple zeros. Together with the endpoint and anchor asymptotics proved in the same chapter, these transforms feed the sharp concentration, localization and arithmetic convergence estimates over the primes.

Zeros, growth and the divisor-sum analogue

M(s)=E[Xs]M(s)=E[Xs] for every complex s, with the Euler product converging uniformly on compact sets. All zeros are simple and are exactly the points sℓ,k=(log⁡(ℓ−2)+(2k+1)πi)/log⁡((ℓ−1)/ℓ)sℓ,k​=(log(ℓ−2)+(2k+1)πi)/log((ℓ−1)/ℓ) for odd primes ℓ and integers k. On the circle ∣s∣=r∣s∣=r the maximum modulus is M(−r)M(−r), and log⁡M(−r)=r(log⁡log⁡r+γ)+O(rlog⁡log⁡r/log⁡r)logM(−r)=r(loglogr+γ)+O(rloglogr/logr).

The Mellin transforms of the shifted-prime divisor-sum laws are also entire of order exactly one and infinite type. They are zero-free on Re⁡s≤0Res≤0 and have infinitely many zeros in Re⁡s>0Res>0; for each odd prime ℓ≥5ℓ≥5, the local factor has exactly one simple zero in each disk of an explicit family.

Questions that
remain open.

These open problems concern the Shannon information dimension and other exact constants, concentration, Fourier decay, prime counts, and friable shifted primes.

Information

What law do smooth (friable) p−1p−1 produce?

For fixed u>1u>1, does the law of 1/c(p)1/c(p) over primes p≤xp≤x with P+(p−1)≤x1/uP+(p−1)≤x1/u converge? Further directions

Beyond the main examples

Sharp divisor-sum concentration constants and maximizing locations, and stronger unconditional uniformity for growing moduli, remain open. Certain larger-modulus results in the monograph assume GRH.

Section 13.2 · Chapter 13

A small mathematical dictionary

Support
A point is in the support when every neighborhood of it has positive probability.
Carrier
A set containing the sample with probability one. A very thin carrier can be dense in an interval.
Atom / atomless
An atom is a single value with positive probability. Atomless laws can still be singular.
Absolutely continuous / singular
An absolutely continuous law has a density with respect to length. A singular law puts all its mass on a set of length zero.
The four basic ratio laws
The limiting laws of φ(n)/nφ(n)/n and σ(n)/nσ(n)/n, the abundancy of n, over integers n, and φ(p−1)/(p−1)φ(p−1)/(p−1) and σ(p−1)/(p−1)σ(p−1)/(p−1) over primes p. Here σ is the sum-of-divisors function.
Normal / Liouville
Normality concerns limiting digit-block frequencies. The Liouville property concerns exceptionally close rational approximations.
Erdős–Wintner laws
Limiting probability laws of additive arithmetic functions sampled over integers; shifted-prime analogues use related prime-coordinate models.
Post-quantum cryptography (PQC)
Cryptography intended to withstand attacks by quantum computers. The monograph does not use this term; it appears on this page only as background for the determinant-constrained LWE reduction and the lattice appendix. Nothing in the monograph is a security claim about any scheme.
Prime-indexed Bernoulli convolution
The law of −log⁡X=log⁡2+∑ℓ≥3Bℓωℓ−logX=log2+∑ℓ≥3​Bℓ​ωℓ​, a sum of independent Bernoulli-weighted jumps ωℓ=log⁡(ℓ/(ℓ−1))ωℓ​=log(ℓ/(ℓ−1)) indexed by the odd primes, with P(Bℓ=1)=1/(ℓ−1)P(Bℓ​=1)=1/(ℓ−1); the prime 2 always divides p−1p−1 and contributes the constant log⁡2log2. Classical Bernoulli convolutions use geometric jumps λnλn; here ωℓ≍1/ℓωℓ​≍1/ℓ is nonlacunary and the jumps are linearly independent over QQ.
Rajchman measure
A measure whose Fourier transform tends to zero at infinity. Rajchman measures can be singular; all four basic ratio laws and their logarithmic images are Rajchman. Dimension-zero Rajchman measures carried by Liouville numbers were known from Bluhm and from Bugeaud, and Polasek and Rela realize prescribed slow decay on Liouville carriers; here the four ratio laws have this property with an explicit rate, and their logarithmic images are likewise dimension-zero Rajchman measures giving full mass to the absolutely normal numbers.
Twin-prime singular series S2S2​
S2=2∏ℓ≥3(1−1/(ℓ−1)2)≈1.3203S2​=2∏ℓ≥3​(1−1/(ℓ−1)2)≈1.3203, the Hardy–Littlewood constant in the conjectured count of twin primes. It enters the endpoint constant κend=S2e−γκend​=S2​e−γ, where γ is Euler’s constant.
Generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH)
The Riemann hypothesis for all Dirichlet L-functions. The monograph’s principal results are unconditional; GRH is assumed only for certain quantitative refinements, such as the stretched-exponential Wasserstein upper bound over unrestricted primes, and for uniform extensions to larger modulus ranges. Every such statement is labelled, and unqualified results are unconditional.
Residue number system (RNS)
A representation of integers or matrices by residues modulo several coprime moduli, recombined by the Chinese remainder theorem. The monograph’s sampling theorems describe primitive-root determinant densities when the prime moduli are chosen at random; they do not model computational cost.
Smoothing parameter
For a lattice Λ and error ε, the Micciancio–Regev quantity ηε(Λ)ηε​(Λ): the smallest Gaussian width s at which ∑exp⁡(−πs2∥w∥2)∑exp(−πs2∥w∥2) over nonzero dual vectors w is at most ε.
Fully splitting NTT prime
For N a power of two, an odd prime q≡1 mod 2Nq≡1mod2N, equivalently one over which XN+1=Φ2N(X)XN+1=Φ2N​(X) splits completely, enabling a negacyclic number-theoretic transform of length N.
Dimension arrays
Assignments nx(p)nx​(p) of a finite or infinite matrix dimension to each prime p. Several convergence statements hold uniformly over such arrays, so finite n×nn×n matrices are covered, not only the n→∞n→∞ limit. Finite dimensions are close to the limit: 0<cn(p)/c(p)−1≤C∗p−(n+1)0<cn​(p)/c(p)−1≤C∗​p−(n+1) with the optimal constant C∗≈2.9255C∗​≈2.9255 (Corollary 12.4).
Fourier dimension
A dimension defined by the strength of polynomial Fourier decay. Decay only on logarithmic scales can coexist with Fourier dimension zero.
CkCk / HsHs / LqLq
CkCk means k continuous derivatives; HsHs measures square-integrable fractional smoothness; LqLq measures integrability of the q-th power.
∼∼ / ≍≍ / ≪≪ / OO / ⇒⇒
∼∼ means ratio tends to one; ≍≍ means bounds by positive constant multiples; ≪≪ and O denote an upper bound up to a constant; ⇒⇒ denotes convergence in distribution in probability-law formulas, and logical implication in the Sophie Germain statement.
Explore the monograph

Results and references

“Proved” means stated and proved in the monograph. This companion distinguishes those claims from conjectures, open questions, numerical evaluations and schematic illustrations.

Keywords and classification

Keywords (from the monograph): shifted primes, Erdős–Wintner laws, totient and divisor-sum distributions, Hausdorff and packing dimensions, Shannon information dimension, quantization dimensions, absolutely normal Liouville numbers, concentration functions, Fourier decay, Fourier amplitudes, absolute continuity, learning with errors, cyclotomic codifferents, lattice smoothing parameter.

Subject: number theory; harmonic analysis of singular measures; Bernoulli convolutions; cyclotomic lattices. Related terms used on this page: prime-indexed Bernoulli convolutions, Rajchman measures, Jessen–Wintner pure-type theorem, continued fractions, abundancy, probabilistic number theory, primes in arithmetic progressions, Sophie Germain and safe primes, primitive-root determinant densities, random matrices over finite fields, learning with errors (LWE), number-theoretic transform (NTT) primes, residue number systems, lattice-based post-quantum cryptography.

Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 11N60; Secondary 11H06, 11J82, 11K16, 11K65, 11L20, 11N13, 11N56, 11R18, 28A78, 42A38, 60E05, 94A17, 94A34, 94A60.

Corollary 11.8 · Normal Liouville fields

Independent samples from the four ratio laws almost surely generate a field of infinite transcendence degree whose irrational elements are all absolutely normal and Liouville. Every fixed nonconstant rational image with real coefficients is Rajchman and almost surely absolutely normal.

Theorem 12.10 · A certificate from partial factorization

The true reciprocal determinant density lies between explicit lower and upper bounds using the small-factor product, rough-cofactor envelope V, and rational enclosures of the Euler-product factor. Complete factorization of the rough cofactor is unnecessary.

Theorem 12.17 · Decision LWE with a prescribed determinant law

Under the stated exact-sampling assumptions, a distinguisher of advantage ε for n×nn×n matrix LWE with secret uniform conditional on its nonzero determinant yields a vector-LWE distinguisher in dimension n−1n−1 with advantage ε/nε/n, preserving the entrywise error law. This independent decision-reduction branch is relevant to lattice-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC); it is not a protocol-security theorem.

proved

Appendix D · Independent lattice-geometry branch

Building on Kitaoka’s minimum and minimal-vector classification, this independent appendix determines the second and third distinct squared norms of type-A tensor products, classifies the second shell and gives cyclotomic codifferent shell data and smoothing estimates. It is independent of the limiting-law and certified-search proofs.

proved

Theorem D.1 · The first three type-A tensor shells

The squared minimum 2k2k and classification of minimal vectors as pure root tensors are due to Kitaoka. The monograph determines the second and third distinct squared norms. With at least two non-A1A1​ factors, the second squared-length ratio is 3/23/2; it classifies this shell as non-pure six-cycle tensors and gives its multiplicity.

proved

Theorem D.3 · Cyclotomic second-length ratios

The ratio of the second distinct nonzero squared norm to the minimum is 3/23/2 when the conductor has at least two distinct odd prime divisors, 3 for conductors 3 and 6, and 2 otherwise.

proved

Theorem D.7 · Uniform smoothing from dual-shell gaps

For a full-rank lattice with a known gap between its first two distinct dual lengths, explicit hypotheses bound the smoothing parameter above and below by a first-shell approximation. A stated exponent condition gives uniform exponential closeness.

Theorem 9.8 · Shared-coordinate two-dimensional slow-jump laws

For distinct A,B>0A,B>0, the joint integer or shifted-prime law of (fA,fB)(fA​,fB​), using the same prime activations, is absolutely continuous on R2R2. Corollary 11.10 · Normal Liouville fields at distinct shifts

The joint limiting totient-ratio model at any countable sequence of distinct nonzero integer shifts almost surely generates a field of infinite transcendence degree whose irrational elements are all absolutely normal and Liouville. Each fixed nonconstant rational image with real coefficients is Rajchman and almost surely absolutely normal. The coordinates share residue variables and are dependent.

Theorem 6.10 · Integer-to-shifted-prime extreme-tail transfer

For reciprocal-totient or divisor-sum ratios, the shifted-prime tail above t equals t times the integer tail, with relative error ON(t−N)ON​(t−N) for every fixed N>0N>0. Conditional on exceeding t, the entire prime-valuation laws in the two models differ in total variation by ON(t−N)ON​(t−N).

Corollary 2.8 · Deshouillers’ support criterion

For a positive multiplicative g whose values g(p−1)g(p−1) have a continuous limiting probability law, its support is exactly the closure of the values at odd primes; the CDF increases across an open interval exactly when it contains such a value. Deshouillers conjectured the criterion; the restricted case 0<g≤10<g≤1 was announced earlier.

proved

Section 12.5 · Determinant-constrained LWE and secret-sharing moduli

Sets out the vector, square-matrix, uniform-secret and PRIM-LWE models of SYD21 and bounds the reciprocal density of the prescribed moduli p=2m+1p=2m+1 (Proposition 12.14). The monograph records that its factor-n reduction (Theorem 12.17) changes the dimension by one, and that the same-dimension factor npnp of Corollary 12.18 does not establish the O(n2)O(n2) advantage factor asserted in SYD21 Theorem 10 for unrestricted moduli; that the proof of that theorem specifies no procedure extracting a PRIM-LWE instance from the hidden secrets; and that the bounded-norm determinant encoding of SYD21 §8.2 is not shown to produce the uniform primitive-determinant secrets the theorem assumes. Neither of the monograph’s reductions establishes the security of that protocol.

Reading notes

The monograph contains the full statements, hypotheses and historical references. Statement numbering may differ between arXiv versions.

The finite-product probabilities and NTT acceptance fractions use exact integer arithmetic. Decimal display values are rounded. Buchstab values below θ=13θ=31​ use numerical integration; the other displayed regimes use explicit formulas. The entropy and Fourier panels are explicitly schematic.

The basic limiting laws are classical: Schoenberg (1928) proved the continuous integer totient law and Erdős (1939) its singularity; Davenport (1933) treated the integer divisor-sum ratio; for shifted primes, Barban, Vinogradov and Levin obtained normalized laws for strongly additive functions of Kubilius class H, Kátai treated p+1p+1 and p−1p−1, and Hildebrand’s general theorem uses Bombieri–Vinogradov. Card headings in the list above describe each result in the companion’s words; the tooltip on each theorem number gives the monograph’s own title. The companion highlights their finer geometry, concentration, Fourier behavior and arithmetic applications. Classical inputs include the Kawabata–Dembo rate–distortion identity and Kitaoka’s minimal-vector theorem; “proved” does not by itself claim historical priority. The source text gives full attribution and proof assumptions. This companion is selective; it does not reproduce every generalization, proof or appendix. Section 08 and the expandable panels marked with theorem numbers cover the explicit extremal bounds, random prime bases, growing moduli, certificate sharpness, the Mellin transform and the re-examined earlier reduction.
